source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Remain in the current location regardless of exits because movement is more dangerous than sheltering during any active-shooter event.","B":"Confront the attacker immediately whenever possible, because physical resistance is recommended before evacuation or hiding.","C":"Call emergency services first and remain exposed while waiting, because evacuation should not occur until law enforcement arrives.","D":"Evacuate if a safe route is available, hide or secure shelter if evacuation is not possible, and fight only as a last resort."}}
source_row.rationale: The "Run, Hide, Fight" framework (promoted by DHS and widely adopted in healthcare active shooter training) teaches individuals to prioritize evacuation ("run") if it can be done safely, then hiding/sheltering in place if evacuation is not possible, with fighting back as a last resort only when directly confronted and facing imminent danger to life.
source_row.source_detail: CISA Options for Consideration: run when possible, hide when evacuation is not possible, and fight as a last resort when confronted with an active shooter. Current CISA active-shooter resource reviewed 2026-08-15. Reviewed 2026-08-15.
